title: Properness is reflected by nilpotent base change
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$, and let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $f_0:Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Then $f$ is proper if and only if $f_0$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No flatness, finite-type, or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, part (7); Spec(A/I) is a finite order thickening of Spec(A), and the source square is cartesian by construction.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, $i:S_0\to S$ and $j:Y_0\to Y$. If $f$ is proper, its base change $f_0$ is proper by clause (1) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change].

source.place: Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, proof of (7), using (2) and Tag 09ZV, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms, parts (3), (4), (6).

proof.text: Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] with $K=I$, first to $X=S$ with identity structure map, then to $X=Y$ with structure map $f$. Thus $i,j$ are closed immersions with ideals $I\mathcal O_S$ and $I\mathcal O_Y$, and $(I\mathcal O_S)^N=I^N\mathcal O_S=0$, $(I\mathcal O_Y)^N=I^N\mathcal O_Y=0$. Taking $n=N-1\geq0$ gives finite order thickenings by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Indeed on each affine chart every element of the defining ideal is nilpotent, so the ideal lies in every prime; the closed immersions are surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism] both are homeomorphisms and remain surjective homeomorphisms after every scheme base change. The pullback projections give $fj=if_0$.

source.place: Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, proof of (7), using (2) and Tag 09ZV, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms, parts (3), (4), (6).

proof.text: Assume now $f_0$ proper. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $f_0$ is separated, universally closed, quasi-compact and locally of finite type. The square defining $Y_0$ is cartesian and $i$ is a finite order thickening. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-lft-cartesian] to this square: $f$ is locally of finite type. This is precisely where nilpotence, rather than just equality of underlying spaces, is needed.

source.place: Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, proof of (7), using (2) and Tag 09ZV, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms, parts (3), (4), (6).

proof.text: To reflect separatedness, regard $Y_0,Y,S_0,S$ as their representable algebraic spaces over $S$ using [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. This does not change the diagonals: on each test scheme, their fibre products have the same universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. A scheme closed immersion gives a closed immersion of these spaces, since every scheme test is a base change and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] applies; the converse follows by testing with the target scheme itself. The topology computed from the identity scheme atlas is the original topology. Consequently $i,j$ are thickenings of algebraic spaces, and the separatedness of $f_0$ is exactly separatedness in [lem-sfb-space-thickening-topological-properties]. In that clause substitute $(X,X\prime,Y,Y\prime)=(Y_0,Y,S_0,S)$, $(i,j)=(j,i)$ and $(f,f\prime)=(f_0,f)$, with base scheme $B=S$. Its commutativity hypothesis is exactly $fj=if_0$, so it gives separatedness of $f$; testing its diagonal with $Y\times_S Y$ gives the required scheme closed immersion. Only the separatedness clause is used; no assertion identifying scheme and algebraic-space universal closedness is needed.

source.place: Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, proof of (7), using (2) and Tag 09ZV, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms, parts (3), (4), (6).

proof.text: Quasi-compactness can be read directly on the homeomorphisms $i,j$. If $U\subseteq S$ is an affine open, $i^{-1}(U)$ is a quasi-compact open of $S_0$, and $j$ identifies $f_0^{-1}(i^{-1}(U))$ homeomorphically with $f^{-1}(U)$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], a finite affine open cover of $i^{-1}(U)$ has quasi-compact inverse images under $f_0$; their finite union is $f_0^{-1}(i^{-1}(U))$, hence quasi-compact. Its homeomorphic image $f^{-1}(U)$ is therefore quasi-compact. Thus $f$ is quasi-compact. For universal closedness take any scheme $T\to S$, and put $T_0=T\times_S S_0$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $(Y\times_S T)\times_T T_0\cong Y_0\times_{S_0}T_0$. The maps $T_0\to T$ and $Y_0\times_{S_0}T_0\to Y\times_S T$ are base changes of $i$, hence homeomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism]. For a closed subset $C\subseteq |Y\times_S T|$, take its inverse image $C_0$ under this homeomorphism. Since $f_0$ is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], its base change to $T_0$ sends $C_0$ to a closed subset of $T_0$. Write $p:Y\times_S T\to T$, $p_0:Y_0\times_{S_0}T_0\to T_0$ for the projections and $h:T_0\to T$ for the homeomorphism. Then $p(C)=h(p_0(C_0))$: commutativity gives the inclusion from right to left, and surjectivity of the upper homeomorphism lifts each point of $C$ to $C_0$, giving the reverse inclusion. This set is closed because $h$ is a homeomorphism. This proves universal closedness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, proof of (7), using (2) and Tag 09ZV, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms, parts (3), (4), (6).

proof.text: We have obtained local finite type, quasi-compactness, separatedness and universal closedness of $f$. The first two give finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and these properties give properness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Together with step 1 this proves both implications. No step assumed flatness or Noetherianity, nor finite type of $f$ in advance.
